[quote=oceanice_republics;60215951]C.C.N. Election Report - After the coup, election results rock the new republic  a new party has been voted into the federal parliamentary republic. 

With the recent coup behind them, a long decade of once ruling the Semi-Authoritarian government has come to a close. This marked the first-ever election to be held by the people and not by the government's influence in the system. Oceanice will be forever free from the once authoritarian government that threatened peace and balance of the republic. 

Election Results

The Federal Liberal Republic or F.L.R. has won 34% and 162 seats. Led by Seyra Velnarik, the F.L.R. emerged as the strongest party in the new parliament. Campaigning on promises of civil freedoms, social democracy, and transparent governance, the F.L.R. captured the hopes of a population longing for stability and liberty.

The United Democracy Conservative Front or U.D.C.F. has won 29% and 139 seats.  Marcus Helviks conservative-nationalist U.D.C.F. ran a strong campaign emphasizing security, tradition, and rebuilding the Republics economy through order and discipline. A bitter rival of the F.L.R.

The Free Democratic Coalition or F.D.C. has won 14% and 68 seats.
Elira Kohnstadts centrist liberal party attracted younger voters and business-minded citizens seeking a balance between reform and enterprise.

The Undieted Republic Union or U.R.U. has won 10% and 47 seats.
Dmitrek Varrnos populist party leaned nationalist and pragmatic, drawing voters frustrated with ideological extremes.

The Social Democratic Republic or S.D.R. has won 7% and 32 seats.
Jonas Rekkards social democrats fought for labor rights and welfare protections, resonating in industrial sectors.

The Federation Union Worker or F.U.W./U.W.U. has won 4% and 19 seats. Tarya Linsovs workers party struggled to gain mass support, though it still maintains a strong influence in the factory District.

The Pro-Humanist Capitalist Party or P.H.C.P. has won 2% and  11 seats. Viktor Draemholts far-right, elitist agenda gained traction only among wealthier urban voters.

Seyra Velnarik has officially become the first Furry President of the Oceanice Republic, with the Federal Liberal Republic or F.L.R. securing the majority vote in the nations first free and democratic election following the collapse of the semi-authoritarian regime. With widespread public support, the F.L.R. has taken its place as the leading political force in the republic, promising reforms, inclusivity, and a break from the shadows of the past government.

Celebrations have erupted across the major cities as supporters gather in the streets, waving banners and chanting for freedom, progress, and unity. Opposition parties have acknowledged the results, though some caution that the path ahead will be difficult as the country recovers from decades of authoritarian control.[/quote]

The council and people of Nordiheim would like to congratulate the nation of Oceanice Republics on a succesful election and hope its future will bring them prosperity as a true democracy.

Okay [quote=oceanice_republics;60209995][i][b]Welkis City[/b]

[u]Command Bunker beneath the Central Mall District[/u]

The concrete walls shook as muffled gunfire echoed above. Hikman Eikira leaned over the steel operations table, maps of Wellgoes Isle scattered with red and blue markers. Sweat rolled down his temples as his adjutant rushed in, face pale. sounds like a breakup

Adjutant: Governor Eikira, the mall district has turned. Furry partisansarmed, organized, theyve taken over the east wing. Loyalists are fighting inside the shops and upper levels. Reports of Molotovs, improvised explosives Its spreading fast.

Hikman Eikira: slams his fist on the table Damn it! I told them to scour the city weeks ago. You let them burrow into our streets like rats! Now they strike at the heart of my city, while the mainland burns in treachery.

He walked to the underground slit window, watching smoke rise from the central boulevard. Sounds of shouting and machine-gun fire filtered down from above.
Communications Officer: Sir, we still hold the SRBM batteries. But loyalist morale is cracking. Many have families from off northern mainland. If they believe the city is falling, they might
Hikman Eikira: snaps They will obey my orders. Anyone caught hesitating will be executed as a traitor. Deploy the Leopards to the mall perimeterseal the district off entirely. I want that marketplace drowned in fire if we must!

Another blast thundered, rattling the room. A runner stumbled in, clothes torn, helmet cracked.
Runner: Governor! Theyve taken the tram station! Furries armed with captured weapons are pushing into the mall concourse. Civilians are joining them, our men cant hold them back without armor support!

Hikman Eikira (coldly, after a long pause)

 Then drown them. Gas the lower tunnels, collapse the exits, burn them alive if we must. Welkis belongs to me, and if these creatures think they can rise, well show them Oceanice steel.
He turned to his adjutant, voice lowering but coldly.

Still if the paratroopers are truly coming, this uprising may not be a coincidence. They may be baiting us, drawing our armor away from the SRBMs. If I fall for it, the missiles are lost.
He straightened, grim, his shadow falling over the map of the island.

Very well. Hold the SRBMs at all costs. Sacrifice Welkis if we must. Let the furries choke on their own smoke and rubble. When reinforcements come, this island will still answer to me.[/i]

[spoiler=[b]Maasis funeral[/b]]
It is a foggy morning. As the miserable weather descends upon Astan city square, a feeling of mourning is felt throughout the country for today is the funeral of Maasi Sarica, Astanirs most revered leader. He died as one of the thousands of victims to the Llyndorran Flu and as a result masks are mandatory for attending the funeral. Despite this, hundreds of sideline watchers do not wear masks as they cannot afford them, a testament to Astanirs collapsing economy and degrading living conditions.

At 10:00 am sharp, the military troops would begin their procession. Maasis coffin would be held inside an armoured vehicle, surrounded by a variety of other armoured vehicles, tanks and infantry, whilst the band would march behind them playing Astanirs national anthem.

The procession would begin in the city centre, before turning down various streets to reach the parliamentary offices where Maasi was to be buried underneath a tree, however like all things in the country as of late, this did not go as planned. Upon reaching the end of Malesi street, the procession would turn right onto Sakaksi street, expecting to see a cobbled street lined with onlookers, leading straight forwards, but instead they would be greeted by an armada of infantry, tanks, armoured vehicles and armed police guards, all aiming at the procession. Then, almost half of the procession would break away and begin surrounding the remaining troops and Maasis coffin.

Around a week earlier, when news got out that Maasi had been struck by the Llyndorran virus, a disgruntled general within Astanirs army had spotted the perfect opportunity. General Kaiwai had always been opposed to Astanirs opening up to the world. He had also always been annoyed that he could never seem to rise up Astanirs ranks. Even after Maasi died he was not offered a promotion, despite having all of the requirements. So, he decided that a coup would be necessary to secure the future of Astanir. He had spent the week gathering like-minded troops, being careful not to catch the attention of the council. He succeeded. He managed to round up over 70% of Astanirs armed forces to his cause and now his effort would culminate in yet another coup upon Astanirs government.

DROP YOUR WEAPONS NOW! Shouted several soldiers towards the procession.
WE WILL OPEN FIRE!
No response.
*BANG* *BANG* *BANG*
The crowd flee as bullets ricocheted from the armoured vehicles. Windows shattered, spraying glass shards everywhere. The remaining procession would begin firing back, but with no luck. The soldiers would slowly move in, taking out vehicle be vehicles until they got to the Center and broke into Maasis vehicle. The coffin would be smashed open with combat knives and the body stolen. The troops would then begin to move towards revolution street, carrying Maasis body
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Revolution street[/b]]
Revolution street had stood as a testament to the Astaniran civil war, since the wars conclusion in 1973. At the end of the street usually stood tall statues of great nationalist leaders, holding the heads of the deposed communist leaders. Today however, at the end of the street was a line of tanks and armoured vehicles, boasting Astaniran flags, but not the usual one, a new one now in use by the isolationist forces. They stood as a show of power, whilst other forces begun the takeover of parliament.

News quickly spread of the ongoing coup and loyalist forces, made up of those who had not defected from the army under General Kaiwai, began grouping together to hopeful stop the coup. They would proceed to march towards revolution street to face off against the defectors. They would arrive just 2 hours after the coup began to find the armed defectors standing upon Maasis mutilated body. As soon as the defectors caught sight of the incoming loyalist forces, they took positions and initiated a shoot out.

Bullets would fly back and forth for hours, but the defectors would be able to eventually push back the loyalists, who would eventually escape out of the city. The defectors would not pursue them, as per orders from General Kaiwai.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Parliament[/b]]
The defected isolationist forces would quickly storm the parliament offices. The two remaining military council members, General Alonir and General Bilgin, would be hiding in their offices. As soon as they were notified of the situation, guards would begin blocking the doors to their office and standing guard, but they did not realise that Kaiwai had managed to recruit those from even within the ranks of their personal guard unit. 

The defectors would quickly get past the loyalist guards at the doors, with sheer manpower and with help from behind. Along the way they would slowly gather up all of the non-loyalist guards within the building, until they reached the office. A fight would commence between the door guards and the defectors.

Inside the office, two guards would move from their allocated positions, taking the other three by surprise and quickly neutralising them. They would then proceed to take the two generals captive, one each. The generals had lost all of their strength and fighting skills for years of executive power and would be quickly capture and tied to their chairs. The two guards inside would then unblock the doors and begin firing from behind, quickly killing all of the loyalist guards. Parliament was theirs.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Aftermath[/b]]
With the entire city now under isolationist forces and the two council members captured, General Kaiwai would order their execution. 2 days after the coup began, The two generals would be shot on live television for all those with enough money to see.

Later, General Kaiwai would announce to the public that Astanir had [b]formally withdrawn from the treaty of Astan[/b], effectively collapsing the short-lived axis.

Kaiwai knew in the coming days that protests and counter-attacks would come, but he would be prepared
[/spoiler]

[nation]Shahzada[/nation] RP
